title: Trust no inbox.
subject: PNN: The Pyro Posse can't stand the mail. A study says nobody wants your data.
preheader: A complaint, a poster, a can of meat, and a study on why you taped your camera.

featuredCase.teaser: **The Pyro Posse can start a fire but can't stand the mail.** One complaint, one very busy poster, and a sudden question about witches. Clueso has the incident log. The pumpkins have declined to comment. *They are on fire, but they have declined.*

sections.heading:
Study finds nobody wants your data.
You are still taping the camera.

runs.text: The
Institute for Alarming Conclusions
surveyed 1,000 neighbors about the black market, the dark web, data leaks, and anyone who asks how their dog is doing.
The findings are in. The dark web has your email address. It does not want it. It has tried to give it back.
Twice.
Researchers report that the average neighbor believes a shadowy figure in a hoodie is bidding on their grocery list. The hoodie, on inspection, was the neighbor's own. The "bidding" was a coupon.
The hoodie was not impressed either.

sections.heading: The numbers, such as they are

items.text: **Neighbors with tape over their webcam.** The remaining 6% have a second piece of tape over the first, 'for depth.'
**Estimated black-market value of an average email address.** Buyers requested a refund and a nicer address.
**Smart speakers that deny listening.** Which is exactly what a listening speaker would say. Researchers put tape over it. The speaker has *noted* this.
**Average time spent choosing a 'strong' password.** It is still the dog's name, followed by a 1.
**Witches found in this newsletter.** PNN checked twice. It also checked the unsubscribe link, which was a link.

runs.text: Lead finding:
you are not a high-value target. You are a medium-value neighbor with a good casserole recipe. The black market has seen the recipe. It is
fine.

sections.heading:
Are you suspicious enough?
(Yes. Keep going.)

runs.text: 01 / You taped your camera.
Understandable. You have also taped the sticker of a camera on your laptop,
for symmetry.
02 / You read the entire privacy policy.
In the dark. With a flashlight you have not connected to the internet. The flashlight is also suspicious.
03 / You use a different email address for every website.
One of them is for newsletters. It is called dontemailme_ever9. It is the only address that has ever been emailed.
04 / You whisper near the refrigerator.
The refrigerator has noticed. The refrigerator has
opinions.
05 / You checked this newsletter for witches.
See PNN-006. Ask the pumpkins. They are still on fire.
Scoring:
any number of checks means you are doing great. The tape is fine.
Keep the tape.

sections.kicker: A NOTE FROM THE SOURCES DESK
sections.heading:
PNN's perfect record.
(Sources have been consulted. Quietly.)

runs.text: PNN would like to note, as a side matter, that it has
never
had a data breach, a leaked source, or a misplaced casserole recipe. Its record on keeping sources safe is so clean that it has been nominated, twice, for the
Golden Redaction Award for Keeping Sources Safe
and once for the
Medal of Mostly Impeccable Journalistic Integrity.
PNN did not win. The jury called the record "suspiciously flawless," which Clueso has chosen to treat as
a win.
The sources, for the record, are safe, unnamed, and slightly overfed.
Rule 8 still stands:
never share names, addresses, or phone numbers with outside groups. PNN does not sell, trade, or auction personal information, including to the black market, which has been checking.
PNN will not be taking questions about the casserole.

tickerItems.text: Tape futures steady. Webcam tape futures unchanged, but extremely nervous.
New PNN study finds nobody wants your data. Subjects respond by taping the camera. Researchers are 'a little hurt.'
Neighbors score themselves on PNN's 'Are you suspicious enough?' quiz. Everyone passes. Clueso says that is exactly what suspicion looks like.
